innova-destroyer.tagline: A 12-speed distance driver for big arms and forehands. The catch: fresh beefy runs hook left fast.
innova-destroyer.bottom: Built for strong arms, forehand bombs and wind. Beginners and slower arms should skip it.

yes.title: Wind and utility
yes.t: Champion, Metal Flake and Halo runs ==fight headwinds with a hard hook==.

yes.title: Sidearm bomber
yes.t: Serves as ==a max-distance flex driver off the forehand==, best once beat in.

yes.title: Repeatable flight
yes.t: Lands ==in a tight spread throw after throw==, out to about 450 ft.

no.title: Beefy out of the box
no.t: Fresh, max-weight and Metal Flake runs can ==hook hard left early==.

no.title: Run-to-run swings
no.t: Splits opinion: copies range ==from flippy to beefy==, even in one plastic.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Slower arms get ==instant spike hyzers and short drives==.

mvp-trail.tagline: A 10-speed driver for easy, straight distance. The catch: runs vary from overstable to very flippy.
mvp-trail.bottom: Great for intermediate arms wanting distance. Skip it if you need every copy to fly the same.

yes.title: Fairway precision
yes.t: Neutron and Proton ==hold straight lines through tight woods==.

yes.title: Easy distance
yes.t: Often ==the longest disc in the bag==, with less effort than wide rims.

yes.title: Sidearm ready
yes.t: Takes ==hard forehands without rolling over==.

no.title: Run lottery
no.t: Copies ==range from overstable to wildly flippy==, even within Neutron.

no.title: Flips at speed
no.t: Light, Fission and some fresh copies ==turn over and can roll==.

no.title: Wear changes it
no.t: Use moves it ==from stable to straight, then to a roller==.

innova-mamba.tagline: A glidey, very understable 11-speed for easy distance. The catch: power throws flip it hard and burn.
innova-mamba.bottom: A great distance step-up for slower and developing arms. Big arms wanting a fade should skip it.

yes.title: Slow-arm distance
yes.t: Massive turn and glide ==carry developing throwers much farther==.

yes.title: Shot-shaping tool
yes.t: Steep hyzers ==pop up flat and glide a long way==; anhyzers become rollers.

yes.title: Premium-plastic control
yes.t: Halo Star ==holds lines without turning and burning==.

no.title: Big arms overpower it
no.t: Flat, powered throws ==flip hard and burn==, worst in GStar or Champion.

no.title: Numbers mislead
no.t: Splits opinion: copies can ==fly far more stable than -5 turn==, Halo especially.

no.title: Learning curve
no.t: Each copy ==flies a little differently==, so it takes time to figure out.

latitude-64-river.tagline: A huge-glide fairway driver for easy straight distance. The catch: power or headwinds flip it over.
latitude-64-river.bottom: Ideal for newer, slower and senior arms. Power throwers should skip it.

yes.title: Effortless carry
yes.t: Massive glide ==keeps low-power throws aloft== with a soft finish.

yes.title: Tight-line tool
yes.t: Flips to flat and ==holds anhyzer and tunnel lines== through woods.

yes.title: Beginner friendly
yes.t: Easy, straight hyzer flips ==suit newer and senior throwers==.

no.title: Big arms flip it
no.t: Power or a headwind can ==turn it over and burn==.

no.title: Beats in fast
no.t: Wear ==makes it flippy within months==, fastest in Retro plastic.

no.title: Plastics differ
no.t: Opto Orbit and Gold Ice ==fly stiffer than Gold Line==; max-weight is straighter.

innova-teebird3.tagline: A flat, stable 8-speed fairway with a reliable fade. The catch: Halo runs fly far beefier than Star.
innova-teebird3.bottom: A dependable control driver for intermediate and advanced arms. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Power-proof control
yes.t: Pushes straight at speed, then ==finishes with a dependable fade==.

yes.title: Sidearm workhorse
yes.t: Halo and Champion ==hold long flex lines off the forehand==.

yes.title: Into the breeze
yes.t: Flat, stiff GStar and Champion ==punch through headwinds==.

no.title: Plastic matters
no.t: Splits opinion: Halo copies can ==fly far beefier== than Star or color-glow runs.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Champion and Halo copies ==drop hard for slower arms== until beaten in.

no.title: Loses its finish
no.t: Star copies ==wear toward understable==, while Halo holds up for a year.

innova-teebird.tagline: A classic straight-to-fade 7-speed fairway. The catch: new Champion runs are too stiff for slow arms.
innova-teebird.bottom: A lifelong workhorse for intermediate arms and up. Slow arms should skip new Champion runs.

yes.title: Classic control
yes.t: Holds straight through tree lines, then ==fades reliably at the end==.

yes.title: Ages well
yes.t: One copy can ==be thrown through its whole life==, from beefy to Leopard-like.

yes.title: Weather ready
yes.t: Champion and heavy copies ==push through headwinds== and stay true.

no.title: Stiff for slow arms
no.t: New Champion and some Star copies ==fly too overstable== for modest power.

no.title: Copy lottery
no.t: Copies ==range from Leopard-like to Firebird-like== off the shelf.

no.title: Can lose its fade
no.t: Worn Pro and some Star copies can ==turn over, even in a light headwind==.

westside-harp.tagline: An overstable approach putter with a trusty fade. The catch: BT plastics can straighten out quickly.
westside-harp.bottom: A go-to upshot and wind disc for most levels. Skip BT plastic if you want a lasting hard fade.

yes.title: Dependable finish
yes.t: Thrown hard, it ==won't turn over and fades left on time==.

yes.title: Wind fighter
yes.t: VIP and Tournament runs ==fly through strong headwinds== as if calm.

yes.title: Forehand trust
yes.t: Clean sidearm releases give ==a reliable left finish on upshots==.

no.title: Loses its bite
no.t: BT plastics ==straighten as they season==, while VIP holds its fade.

no.title: Less fade than rated
no.t: Domey and some premium copies ==fly straighter than a 0/3==.

no.title: Grip complaints
no.t: The deep beaded rim can ==catch fingers and add flutter==.

axiom-hex.tagline: A straight, glidey midrange with a soft finish. The catch: Eclipse runs can fly quite overstable.
axiom-hex.bottom: A do-everything straight mid for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you throw hard into wind.

yes.title: Pinpoint control
yes.t: Holds ==dead-straight lines with a soft finish==, even in gusts.

yes.title: Long for a mid
yes.t: Glides ==close to fairway-driver distance==.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: Grippy plastic and a slim rim ==release cleanly on touch shots==.

no.title: Plastic changes it
no.t: Splits opinion: Fission flies neutral while ==Eclipse can run quite overstable==.

no.title: Overpowered flips
no.t: Hard throws into headwind can ==turn it over==, and wind pushes it around.

no.title: Can hook late
no.t: Glide ==magnifies the fade== when thrown high.

discraft-buzzz.tagline: The benchmark straight midrange for every level. The catch: new copies fade more at lower power.
discraft-buzzz.bottom: A staple mid for beginners through intermediates. Skip it if you want a zero-fade straight flyer.

yes.title: Benchmark control
yes.t: Holds ==straight lines with a gentle checkup== across every plastic.

yes.title: Forehand comfort
yes.t: Flat top ==feels steady on sidearm upshots== from awkward spots.

yes.title: Good learning disc
yes.t: Predictable flight ==shows mistakes while still rewarding== newer throwers.

no.title: Fades when fresh
no.t: New copies ==fade more than a Mako3== below full power.

no.title: Wear changes it
no.t: Use can ==strip its finishing fade== within months.

no.title: Plastics differ
no.t: Cryztal, newer and some ESP runs ==fly beefier than classic Z==.

westside-tursas.tagline: A glidey, understable mid for slower arms. The catch: power throws burn it into the ground.
westside-tursas.bottom: Great for slower arms and woods turnovers. Power throwers should skip it.

yes.title: Shot-shaping tool
yes.t: Pops up from hyzer and ==holds sweeping turnover lines== through woods.

yes.title: Beginner friendly
yes.t: Gentle turn and big glide ==give slower arms easy distance==.

yes.title: Steadier options
yes.t: Heavier VIP and Orbit plastic ==resist burning== for precise hyzer flips.

no.title: Flips with power
no.t: Hard throws ==burn it into the dirt==; it rewards low effort.

no.title: Beats in fast
no.t: Tree hits and wear make it ==unreliably flippy== quite quickly.

no.title: Batch differences
no.t: Newer domey runs ==fly more stable== than old flat-top copies.

innova-toro.tagline: A low-glide overstable approach disc. The catch: near-zero glide drops it short for newer arms.
innova-toro.bottom: Built for intermediate and advanced approach games. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Torque-proof finish
yes.t: Fights out of turn and ==dumps right by the target==, even off forced anhyzers.

yes.title: Sidearm go-to
yes.t: Handles ==wobbly and power forehands== on approaches.

yes.title: Wind fighter
yes.t: Low glide ==won't sail past in headwinds==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Near-zero glide ==finds the ground fast== and can leave shots short.

no.title: Mixed comfort
no.t: R-Pro can feel thin, Luster ==too deep to power-grip==, the rim slant odd.

no.title: Bag overlap
no.t: Splits opinion: it fills ==the same role as a Zone==, so pick one.

mvp-deflector.tagline: A meat-hook utility mid for wind and forehands. The catch: too overstable to fly flat or long.
mvp-deflector.bottom: A utility weapon for intermediate and advanced players. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Utility workhorse
yes.t: Fights out of ==any forced anhyzer== and dumps with a big skip.

yes.title: Sidearm muscle
yes.t: Handles ==full-power forehands and sharp doglegs==.

yes.title: Built for storms
yes.t: Drops ==straight out of the sky in heavy wind==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: So overstable it ==can't be made to fly flat== or hold a long line.

no.title: Slow to beat in
no.t: Proton copies ==barely season== and stay beefy for years.

no.title: Limited carry
no.t: Almost no glide ==drops it like a rock==, shortening shots.

axiom-paradox.tagline: An ultra-understable mid for turnovers and hyzer flips. The catch: flat or hard throws roll over.
axiom-paradox.bottom: Great for slower arms and players without a forehand. Power throwers wanting fade should skip it.

yes.title: Shot-shaping tool
yes.t: Steep hyzers ==pop to flat and drift through tight gaps==.

yes.title: Touch-shot ally
yes.t: Turns and ==carries straight at low power== for slow arms.

yes.title: No-flick solution
yes.t: Gives ==forehand-style lines off a backhand== for players without one.

no.title: Big arms overpower it
no.t: Flat or ripped throws ==turn straight into a roller==.

no.title: Finicky control
no.t: Short shots and forehands ==need careful touch==; hyzer flips can go too far.

no.title: Niche bag slot
no.t: Rarely ==earns an everyday spot==, despite doing shots nothing else does.

kastaplast-berg.tagline: A zero-glide approach disc that stops near the pin. The catch: it needs a hard throw to go anywhere.
kastaplast-berg.bottom: A distance-control approach disc for beginners and intermediates. Skip it as a long-range putter.

yes.title: Distance control
yes.t: Runs out of air and ==drops without skipping past==.

yes.title: Angle control
yes.t: Takes power ==without turning over==, holding the release line.

yes.title: Sidearm favourite
yes.t: Concave top ==locks in for soft forehand approaches==.

no.title: No glide
no.t: It ==demands a hard throw== to reach even short targets.

no.title: Tricky to putt
no.t: Can ==be hard to sink== from beyond close range.

no.title: Changes with wear
no.t: K3 and old K1 Soft ==lose late stability== as they beat in.

streamline-pilot.tagline: A glidey, straight throwing putter. The catch: plastic choice swings it from stable to flippy.
streamline-pilot.bottom: A point-and-shoot putter for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you need one stable plastic.

yes.title: Point-and-shoot control
yes.t: Flies ==dead straight with a gentle late fade== on approaches.

yes.title: Easy reach
yes.t: Glide ==carries it as far as most midranges== with little effort.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: Flat top and micro-bead ==sit naturally for forehands and backhands==.

no.title: Run lottery
no.t: Plastic choice ==swings it from overstable to flippy==; Eclipse splits opinion.

no.title: Durability concerns
no.t: Baseline Electron can ==chunk or warp==; worn copies lose stability.

no.title: Flips if forced
no.t: Yanked throws can ==turn and burn==, like a flippier Proxy.

axiom-proxy.tagline: A dead-straight, beadless throwing putter. The catch: stability varies by run and plastic.
axiom-proxy.bottom: A go-to straight putter for beginners and intermediates. Skip it if you want a reliable fade.

yes.title: Point-and-shoot accuracy
yes.t: Holds ==any release angle to the ground== with almost no fade.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: Beadless, low rim ==releases cleanly with a tacky grip==.

yes.title: Two-in-one utility
yes.t: Putts true ==with spin or push== and still drives well.

no.title: Batch lottery
no.t: Stability ==varies by run and plastic==, from Envy-stable to flippy glow.

no.title: Escapes when ripped
no.t: Snapped or flat full-power throws can ==turn over==; it's no hyzer disc.

kastaplast-jarn.tagline: An overstable approach putter with a hard dump. The catch: K1 and K3 fly like different discs.
kastaplast-jarn.bottom: A utility approach disc for intermediate and advanced players. Beginners should skip it.

yes.title: Torque-proof finish
yes.t: Fights out of forced anhyzers and ==dumps hard on every throw==.

yes.title: Forehand favourite
yes.t: Handles ==hard sidearm flicks and flex shots== cleanly.

yes.title: Hand feel
yes.t: K1 and K1 Soft ==grip well and absorb landings==.

no.title: Plastic swings
no.t: K1 and K3 ==fly like different discs==; K3 is shorter with little glide.

no.title: Unusual shape
no.t: Splits opinion: the deep rim and dome ==take time to get used to==.

no.title: Not a first disc
no.t: Little glide and ==a hard dump== suit players who already control approaches.

prodigy-pa-5.tagline: A shallow, understable throwing putter for turnovers. The catch: fast flat throws nearly roll.
prodigy-pa-5.bottom: Great for woods turnovers and newer arms. Skip it if you want a stable putter.

yes.title: Shot-shaping putter
yes.t: Flips up and ==holds slow right-turning lines== through woods.

yes.title: Pleasant in hand
yes.t: Shallow, rounded lip ==feels comfortable and grippy==.

yes.title: Beginner friendly
yes.t: Easy flip-ups and ==floating glide== suit newer and slower arms.

no.title: Hard to rip
no.t: Flat, fast throws ==turn it nearly into a roller==.

no.title: Specialty slot
no.t: Can be ==a niche disc== used only a couple of times a round.

no.title: Plastic changes it
no.t: 750 runs ==fly beefy==, while 300 drifts right the most.
